title: Input Validation and Menu-Based Program
learningObjectives: Describe the purpose and scope of input validation and menu-based program.
Plan the required data, inputs, outputs, and behaviors.
Break the solution into manageable functions or steps.
Implement and test normal, invalid, and boundary cases.
Review the result and explain limitations and improvements.

understand.concept: A menu-based program presents choices, accepts a selection, checks whether the selection is allowed, performs the matching action, and returns to the menu when appropriate. Input validation includes checking type, range, format, and whether a choice is supported. The menu should provide a clear exit route and avoid acting on invalid input.
understand.whyItMatters: This project practices control flow, loops, functions, validation, and user-friendly error handling in a realistic interaction pattern.
understand.analogy: Think of completing a small real-world task by defining the goal, organizing the work, checking each step, and reviewing the finished result.
understand.analogyLimit: Software projects require precise requirements, data and code design, technical testing, and iterative change; the analogy only introduces a workflow.

explain.narrative:
A menu-based program presents choices, accepts a selection, checks whether the selection is allowed, performs the matching action, and returns to the menu when appropriate. Input validation includes checking type, range, format, and whether a choice is supported. The menu should provide a clear exit route and avoid acting on invalid input.

Build incrementally and keep the project scope appropriate for your current skills. The examples illustrate individual design steps; they are not a complete ready-made project. Test your own implementation and document assumptions.

commonMistakes: Starting implementation without defining scope or acceptance criteria.
Combining input, logic, and display in one tangled block.
Claiming features or data persist when they are only in memory.
Adding features before the core workflow works and is tested.

guidedTask.title: Guided Project
guidedTask.instructions: Create a menu with View, Add, and Exit. Each option should call a distinct function. Reject invalid selections and return to the menu after completing an action.
steps: Create a menu with View, Add, and Exit. Each option should call a distinct function. Reject invalid selections and return to the menu after completing an action.
Write a short scope and acceptance checklist.
Test a normal case and at least two edge/error cases.

independentTask.title: Independent Project
independentTask.instructions: Create a menu-driven record manager with at least four actions. Include invalid input handling, a repeat loop, a clear exit option, and tests for every branch.
requirements: Keep the project original and appropriately scoped.
Create a menu-driven record manager with at least four actions. Include invalid input handling, a repeat loop, a clear exit option, and tests for every branch.
Include a short test plan and results.

hints: Keep the menu display separate from actions.
Test each menu branch and invalid selections.
